comparisons.peer_topic: Fair Value Option Election for Non-Structured Liabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company elected the fair value option for certain non-structured liabilities with fixed and floating interest rates to mitigate accounting mismatches and achieve operational simplifications, particularly where interest rate risk may be economically hedged or proceeds are used to purchase financial assets accounted for at fair value.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and C discuss the election of the fair value option for specific financial instruments to manage accounting mismatches. GS discloses that specific time deposits ($44.86 billion) are accounted for at fair value under this option, while C explains the broader rationale for electing the fair value option for non-structured liabilities with fixed and floating interest rates to mitigate accounting mismatches and achieve operational simplifications. Both use the fair value option to address risks or accounting mismatches, though GS focuses on a specific deposit amount and C focuses on the policy rationale for liabilities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment of loans at fair value
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans for which the fair value option is elected are carried at fair value within Trading assets, with changes recognized in earnings. This accounting treatment excludes these loans from the allowance for credit losses and charge-off policies.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS disclose items accounted for under the fair value option. GS specifies that time deposits are accounted for at fair value under the fair value option. MS discloses that loans for which the fair value option is elected are carried at fair value and included in Trading assets. While the instrument types differ (deposits vs. loans), both peers and the target disclose the accounting treatment and inclusion of specific items under the fair value option election.
